title: Chandela Kingdom
capsule: The Chandelas were a Rajput dynasty ruling Jejakabhukti (modern Bundelkhand, central India) from the mid-9th century onward, initially as feudatories of the Gurjara-Pratihara empire. Under Yashovarman (c. 925–950) they became de facto independent, and his successor Dhanga (c. 950–1002) expanded the kingdom while repelling Mahmud of Ghazni's early raids; the dynasty reached its territorial apex under Vidyadhara (c. 1003–1035), who defied both Ghazni and the Paramaras. The Chandelas are best known for the Khajuraho temple complex, largely built between 950 and 1050. Repeated Ghaznavid and later Ghurid pressure eroded their power, and the last Chandela ruler lost Kalinjar fort to Qutb ud-Din Aibak in 1203, though the dynasty lingered as a minor lineage until the 14th century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The broad dynastic sequence and major rulers are well attested through epigraphy and temple inscriptions, but precise territorial limits are uncertain and differ by era.
